data.text: Popmotion is a low-level animation library that powers Framer Motion. It provides tweening, springs, and keyframes.

data.title: Popmotion tween

data.text: The Animation Primitives Under Framer Motion

Popmotion is a functional, unopinionated animation library built from small pieces: a `value` to animate, an `action` such as `tween` or `spring`, and an `easing`. Framer Motion is built on top of it, which is why the concepts look familiar. Using it directly gives fine control without the React wrapper.

data.title: Animate a value with a spring

data.text: Actions are composed and return controls you can stop mid-flight, which is what makes gestures feel responsive: a drag can interrupt an ongoing animation and take over from the current value. `pointer` and `listener` primitives feed gesture input into the same animation system.

data.title: A draggable element
When to use the primitives directly
data.text: Reaching for Framer Motion is the right call in a React app; the primitives matter when you are outside React, driving a canvas, or building a custom gesture interaction where you want to own the loop. Knowing that Framer Motion is a wrapper is itself a good answer, because it explains where the spring configuration comes from.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use Framer Motion for React apps.
